{{Quote|She is one of our best pilots. We cannot afford to lose her.|General Carlist Rieekan|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
'''Samoc Farr''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] regarded as one of the best [[Rebel pilot/Legends|pilots]] serving with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. She grew up on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] in a [[Farr family|family]] that was loyal to [[Chandrilan/Legends|Chandrilan]] native and eventual Rebel Alliance [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] and firmly opposed to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Samoc and her older sister, [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn]], secretly joined the Rebellion after they were reportedly [[Death/Legends|killed]] in a staged [[Transport/Legends|transport]] crash and then taken offworld. The Farr sisters were eventually both assigned to the Rebel [[Alliance High Command/Legends|headquarters]] of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the [[Water/Legends|ice]] planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].

Samoc piloted a modified [[T-47 airspeeder/Legends|T-47 airspeeder]] during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]. Farr's [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]] was shot down during the engagement by an Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] [[Walker/Legends|walker]]. Although badly wounded, she survived and was later evacuated from Hoth aboard the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']] along with her older sister, Echo Base's chief controller. The Farr sisters again survived when the [[Mist Hunter/Legends|''Mist Hunter'']], the craft of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], incapacitated their escape transport during its failed [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] run through the line of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] the planet. After Toryn convinced the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunting duo to rescue Samoc, herself, and the remaining eighty-eight Rebel passengers aboard the ''Bright Hope'', the group was delivered to the Rebellion's underground cell on the planet [[Darlyn Boda/Legends|Darlyn Boda]], where Samoc received medical treatment, including the fabled healing powers of the [[Ankarres Sapphire]], before finally reaching the safety of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] at the Rebels' secret [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] beyond the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|edge]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==Biography==
===Early life and joining the rebellion===
[[File:Hoth_TEA.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hoth, where Samoc and Toryn Farr would be stationed]]
The [[Gender/Legends|female]] Samoc Farr was born and raised on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]],<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> an [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] best known as the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], former [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senatorial]] representative and eventual [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|leader]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="CSWE-Chandrila">{{CSWECite|I|119|Chandrila}}</ref> The [[Farr family]] was loyal to Mothma and staunchly opposed to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. At some point sympathetic [[Chandrilan/Legends|Chandrilan]] authorities helped the Farrs and several more families fake a [[Transport/Legends|transport]] crash in which some of the families' children, including Samoc and her older sister, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn]], were reported [[Death/Legends|killed]]. The ruse provided an opportunity for Samoc and Toryn to slip out of Chandrila and join the Rebellion.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Toryn promised their [[Samoc and Toryn Farr's mother|mother]] that she would take care of Samoc, who was the youngest in the family, and the child always considered the most beautiful, the happiest, and the one with the most promise.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

Samoc became an excellent [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] with the Rebel Alliance<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" />&mdash;one of its best&mdash;and the Farr sisters served in several battles<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> as of the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> by which [[Time/Legends|time]] both were assigned to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], the secret [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters on the remote [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Water/Legends|ice]] planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. At Echo Base Toryn earned a position as [[Communications officer/Legends|chief communications officer]] within the ice facility's command center.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

===Battle of Hoth===
{{Quote|Imperial walker shot me down&mdash;|Samoc Farr, to her sister, Toryn Farr|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
[[File:Rogue_Group_TESB_Manga.jpg|300px|thumb|left|The twelve airspeeders of Rogue Group, including pilot Samoc Farr, attack during the Battle of Hoth.]]
The Empire discovered Echo Base's existence in early 3 ABY, setting off the critical [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]],<ref name="NEC" /> in which the Rebels raced to evacuate their outpost before being overrun by the invading Imperial ground forces of<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> [[Blizzard Force/Legends|Blizzard Force]],<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> attached to the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] personal [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]],<ref name="ESB" /> the [[Death Squadron/Legends|Imperial Death Squadron]]. During the battle Samoc flew with the Alliance's elite [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]] aboard a [[T-47 airspeeder/Legends|T-47 airspeeder]], dubbed "snowspeeders,"<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> tasked with helping to [[Evac Rearguard Action 101|delay]] the advancing line of Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]] [[Walker/Legends|walkers]] long enough to buy time for the Echo Base personnel and equipment to escape Hoth aboard a series of vulnerable [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transports]].<ref name="ESB" /> Samoc flew under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Rogue Six]], joined by the hulking [[Iotran/Legends|Iotran]] [[Vigrat Pomoner]] as her [[Airspeeder/Legends|speeder's]] rear [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]].<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" />

[[File:Imperial_Snowtroopers.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Snowtroopers invading Echo Base during the Battle of Hoth]]
Samoc's snowspeeder was shot down during the battle by an AT-AT,<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> one of seven Rogues to be downed in the engagement.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> Samoc survived, albeit badly wounded,<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> although Pomoner was killed in action.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> She was eventually brought back to Echo Base's main [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] during the late stages of the battle as the final remnants of Rebel personnel rushed to escape the planet before Imperial [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]] descended on the base. Samoc was left lying amidst an assortment of similarly wounded [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel soldiers]] being treated by [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] around the flight deck of the [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], the last remaining Rebel GR-75 medium transport yet to depart the base.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

Toryn soon arrived in the hangar after ordering the final evacuation code signal to the Rebel [[Troop/Legends|troops]] still fighting in the field, only to find the flight deck littered with wounded and dying. Hastily beginning to help load the wounded aboard the ''Bright Hope'', Toryn eventually discovered Samoc lying among the hangar's casualties, injured but still conscious. That Samoc, considering her talents, had been shot down during the battle led Toryn to believe the fight had been truly horrific. Toryn found that Samoc had not received medical treatment in the rush to evacuate and was covered in burns&mdash;her [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and [[Eye/Legends|eyelashes]] were gone, and her [[Limb/Legends|hands]] and face were charred. Toryn carried Samoc aboard the transport, despite the pain she knew it must have caused her younger sister, as snowtrooper [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire exploded around them. The Farr sisters were among the last to board the ''Bright Hope'' before it blasted away from Hoth.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> Although the vessel was designed to safely carry ninety passengers, the ''Bright Hope'' had been cleared of vital equipment to make room for hundreds of evacuees.<ref name="Complete Locations">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

===Survival aboard the ''Bright Hope''===
{{Quote|This goes on and on.''"<br />"''What do you mean?''"<br />"''We're still alive. The Imperials are having a hard time killing us. I'm wondering how the Imperials will finally do it.|Samoc and Toryn Farr, following their survival of the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} blockade run|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
Aboard the final evacuation transport, Toryn strapped her wounded sister into a vacant seat near the boarding hatch and knelt beside her to keep Samoc's body stable for the transport's imminent [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] run through the line of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] waiting in Hoth's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. The ''Bright Hope'' was incapacitated and all but destroyed by concentrated fire from both the Imperial [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] and the [[G-1A starfighter/Legends|G-1A starfighter]] [[Mist Hunter/Legends|''Mist Hunter'']], the personal [[Starship/Legends|starship]] of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], who had entered the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] in the midst of the battle to capture Rebels fleeing the planet. Although a large portion of the ''Bright Hope'' had been completely blown away, killing most aboard, the Farr sisters nevertheless survived, along with 106 others.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

[[File:Brighthope.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The ''Bright Hope'', Samoc Farr's escape transport, leaves Hoth.]]
When Toryn regained consciousness following the transport's ordeal, she found Samoc alive and conscious as well but shaking and moaning&mdash;with her burn wounds still untreated, Samoc had fallen into shock. After Toryn retrieved a brown [[Bantha wool/Legends|bantha-wool]] [[Blanket/Legends|blanket]] that had spilled from an overhead cupboard with which to cover her sister, Samoc grimly whispered to her that the Imperials had failed to kill them, first after Samoc had been shot down over the Hoth battlefield, then having nearly been shot by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] while boarding the transport, and finally having survived the blockade run; she could only wonder how they would finally do it. Toryn refused to think about that possibility but realized that she and her sister, for all the battles they had been through, had never been as close to death as they were at that moment. Instead, Toryn wrapped Samoc tighter in the blanket and went off to search the crippled transport for something with which to treat her burns and perhaps a way to save themselves.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

Searching through the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} damaged interior, Toryn learned that the crippled transport nevertheless still held three accessible, yet malfunctioning, [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]], a possible means of rescue. She also happened upon the medical [[Droid/Legends|droid]] duo of [[2-1B/Legends|2-1B]] and<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> [[FX-7/Legends|FX-7]],<ref name="M. Shayne Bell">Author [[M. Shayne Bell]] inexplicably alternates between referring to 2-1B's droid partner in the story as "Effour-Seven" and "Effex-Seven" several times within the course of a few paragraphs, leading to uncertainty regarding this droid's identity. However, the PC program ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' and the article [[Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth|''Who's Who in Echo Base'']] from [[Star Wars Insider 74|''Star Wars Insider'' 74]] both identify the droid as FX-7, the most commonly recognized partner of 2-1B, as seen in the film {{Film|V}}.</ref> who had previously served in the [[Echo Base medical center/Legends|Echo Base medical lab]]. Toryn ordered the latter, who was equipped with excellent burn-treatment programs, to tend to the wounded Samoc, despite knowing that the droid would obey the command at the expense of bypassing all other Rebel wounded, no matter the extent of their own injuries. She reasoned that if there was a way to survive, she wanted Samoc to live, to honor the promise she had once made to their mother to look out for her younger sister. Still, Toryn hoped that by helping Samoc she would not directly be hurting anyone else.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

Continuing through the transport, taking stock of their situation, Toryn came upon the three escape pods, where a group of Rebels soon restored their functionality. Nevertheless, there were only eighteen available passenger spots in the three pods. A crucial decision thus faced the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} survivors regarding who would go, and who would stay. Toryn eventually compiled a list of all survivors aboard in an effort to determine which Rebels most valuable to the Alliance's cause would be jettisoned back to Hoth aboard the escape pods to be given the best chances of survival. When Toryn broke her list of 108 survivors down to fifty-six, eliminating fifty-two whom the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} medical droids identified as too badly wounded to attempt survival in Hoth's unforgiving environment, Samoc was among those selected to remain aboard. Toryn's leadership abilities earned her a nomination to join the escape pod party, but she refused. Besides knowing she was still needed aboard the transport, Toryn would never leave Samoc behind.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

===An unexpected rescue===
{{Quote|You left one of our best pilots off your list of people to save&mdash;Samoc Farr. You think the Rebellion doesn't need good pilots?|Toryn Farr, to 4-LOM|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
[[File:Toryn-hd.png|thumb|right|300px|Toryn Farr, Samoc's sister]]
With little left to do following the escape pods' jettisoning back to Hoth but prepare for the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} inevitable seizure and boarding by a nearby ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer that had begun mop-up operations on similarly crippled Rebel transports, the ship's remaining passengers began to stockpile weapons and tend to the wounded. They were interrupted, however, when another ship was spotted approaching the ''Bright Hope'', which one Rebel, [[Rory]], identified as the ''Mist Hunter''&mdash;the same craft that had immobilized the ''Bright Hope'', though those aboard were unaware of the role the ''Mist Hunter'' had played in neutralizing the transport.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

The [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunters Zuckuss and 4-LOM soon docked with and boarded the ''Bright Hope'', intending to capture the twenty-six Rebels aboard identified by the [[Imperial Most Wanted List]] as having the largest bounties placed on them. Toryn was foremost on the list. Trying to masquerade as bounty hunters with Rebel connections in one of the largest Imperial bounty hunter guilds, 4-LOM attempted to persuade his twenty-six targets to come with him aboard the ''Mist Hunter'', where he claimed they would be safely transported to the Rebels' [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] at a remote location of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] beyond the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|rim]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In truth, he hoped to infiltrate the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] there and collect on the much more lucrative bounty placed on Rebel [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader. However, none of the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} passengers believed him. Growing desperate, 4-LOM physically ensnared Toryn, the most valuable Rebel, and dragged her aboard his ship and into a secure holding cell. When she protested that the bounty hunters were not there to rescue them, the droid insisted that their efforts were genuine, to which she pointed out that Samoc, one of the Rebellion's most talented pilots, was left off the list of those to be rescued, a blatant lapse in logic. 4-LOM did not respond.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

After the bounty hunting duo realized their guise of an allied rescue attempt had convinced no one and ended in utter failure, Toryn convinced them to take on the remaining passengers still aboard the ''Bright Hope'', including Samoc. And, rather than making the long and hazardous journey to the rendezvous point beyond the reaches of the galaxy, Toryn had convinced their rescuers to deliver them to the Rebel underground on the nearby planet [[Darlyn Boda/Legends|Darlyn Boda]], where Samoc would be able to receive badly needed medical treatment.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

===Deliverance at Darlyn Boda===
{{Quote|Samoc. Do you know what this is?&hellip;Touch it to your burns. It might help you heal&hellip;Did it help you?''"<br />"''I don't know. I feel so different&mdash;in a good way. Rested, maybe?|4-LOM allows Samoc Farr to use the healing powers of the Ankarres Sapphire|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
As the bounty hunters transported their new Rebel passengers to Darlyn Boda, Samoc lay in a cramped rear corner of the confined interior of the ''Mist Hunter'' alongside other Rebel wounded, though her face and hands had since been wrapped in bandages. Looking over her tormented sister, Toryn uneasily doubted her own abilities to lead her comrades on behalf of Samoc. Twice had she put Samoc's well-being above anyone else&mdash;first when she had sent the medical droid to see to Samoc's condition, and then when she tried to get 4-LOM to add her to his list of Rebels to be rescued. What was more, she knew she would do it again, and she knew it was not fair to anyone else. Toryn only hoped she could find someone to take over her command duties once they reached Darlyn Boda.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

[[File:4LOMandZuckuss-TESB.png|thumb|left|300px||Zuckuss and 4-LOM, initial enemies who would in the end help Samoc and Toryn]]
Upon reaching Darlyn Boda, a steamy, crime-ridden world, 4-LOM retrieved the [[Ankarres Sapphire]], a blue gemstone fabled for its reputed healing powers, from a small [[Darlyn Boda jewel shop|jewel shop]], where he had consigned the valuable jewel years before.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> The two bounty hunters and their Rebel consorts spent several [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] on Darlyn Boda<ref>''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' states that it took the ''Millennium Falcon'' "weeks" to reach Bespin on a backup hyperdrive following the Battle of Hoth, thereby providing a rough time frame for any events taking place concurrently with the film {{Film|V}}.</ref> before preparations were made to finally depart for the Alliance Fleet and the secret rendezvous point. Toryn was joined by Samoc and four other ''Bright Hope'' survivors for the trip, while the others would remain behind in the care of Darlyn Boda's Rebel underground. Aboard the ''Mist Hunter'', just prior to lifting off, 4-LOM handed the Ankarres Sapphire to Samoc, allowing her to touch it to her bandaged face wounds in the hope that its healing powers would aid her. Samoc remarked that the sensation the [[Sapphire/Legends|sapphire]] provided her felt strangely physically rejuvenating.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

Samoc and Toryn finally reached the safety of the Rebel fleet at the rendezvous point with the help of Zuckuss and 4-LOM, where they were reunited with family and friends aboard the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] [[Redemption/Legends|''Redemption'']], the fleet's primary [[Hospital ship/Legends|medical frigate]]. They were warmly greeted and informed that they and everyone assigned to the ''Bright Hope'' had been believed dead, or worse. When the Rebel command intended to promote Toryn for her actions in rescuing the passengers aboard the ''Bright Hope'', she attempted to explain to [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] how she had put Samoc's needs ahead of anyone else's. Rieekan, however, only further commended her&mdash;of course she had saved Samoc, for her sister's piloting abilities made her an invaluable asset to the Rebel cause. Samoc, along with her bounty hunting rescuers, attended the ceremony in which Rieekan officially promoted Toryn to the rank of [[Commander/Legends|commander]].<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|We’re still alive. The Imperials are having a hard time killing us.|Samoc Farr, to Toryn|<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />}}
Samoc Farr's harrowing experiences in the Battle of Hoth had a substantial effect on her, and she expressed to her sister, Toryn, of the Imperials' inability to kill them time and again, only wondering when she would finally die.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

The youngest in her family, Farr had always been regarded as the most beautiful, the happiest, and the one with the most promise. Her mother had made her older sister, Toryn, promise to watch out for her. After suffering serious injuries during the Hoth battle, Farr's red hair had been mostly burned away, along with her eyelashes, and she had burns on her hands and face.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

==Skills and abilities==
Samoc Farr was one of the Rebel Alliance's best pilots and an invaluable asset to the Rebellion's cause. After surviving the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} failed blockade run through the Imperial fleet orbiting Hoth, Farr had defied death at the hands of the Empire for the third time over the course of the battle. She had survived being shot down in her snowspeeder, then narrowly missed being blasted by snowtroopers in Echo Base's hangar, and finally found herself among the few fortunate enough to survive the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} virtual destruction.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

==Equipment==
Farr operated a snowspeeder in the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />

==Behind the scenes==
The character Samoc Farr was first created by author [[M. Shayne Bell]] for the short story ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]'', as part of the [[1996]] anthology book ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]''.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" />
